In clean and onion architecture, dependencies always point inward, so inner layers have no knowledge of outer layers.
Domain entities in clean architecture should be framework- and persistence-agnostic, using only plain PHP and possibly the standard library.
Controllers and templates belong to the presentation (delivery/UI) layer; the business-logic layer contains the use cases they call.
In onion architecture, the core (center) is the domain model, with domain services, application services, and outer layers surrounding it.
Tools like deptrac analyze dependencies between layers and fail the build when forbidden dependencies are detected.
A use case should operate on domain objects/DTOs, not framework-specific artifacts like HTTP requests or an EntityManager, which belong in outer layers.
A repository provides a collection-like interface over aggregates/entities while hiding the underlying storage mechanism.
Database access is an infrastructure detail in the outer layer, while domain and use cases depend only on abstractions, so swapping PostgreSQL leaves them unchanged.
An aggregate is a domain-driven design concept: a cluster of domain objects treated as a single consistency unit with a root entity, not merely a database table.
A Value Object is defined by being immutable and equal based on its field values rather than object identity.
In DDD, the aggregate root is the sole external entry point through which all modifications to the aggregate must pass.
In Domain-Driven Design, repositories are defined per aggregate root, since only aggregates are loaded and persisted as whole units.
In Domain-Driven Design, the ubiquitous language is the shared vocabulary used by both developers and domain experts to describe the model.
A namespace defines the scope within which names (a model and its language) are consistent, while the same names outside can refer to other things.
DDD recommends rich domain models that encapsulate behavior and invariants, not anemic models where logic lives only in services.
In DDD, a bounded context defines a boundary within which a model applies, so the same concept may be represented by different classes in different contexts.

Symfony autowiring automatically discovers and injects services, so most services don't need manual declaration.
Twig compiles templates into PHP classes and caches them for reuse across requests.

The APP_ENV environment variable determines the active Symfony environment (e.g., dev or prod).
Symfony controllers must be public methods; private/protected methods cannot be used as routing targets.
Subscribers and listeners receive events in the same dispatch mechanism, and priority is set explicitly—not granted by the SubscriberInterface.
Symfony 6 removed the Guard authenticator system in favor of authenticators based on AuthenticatorInterface.
Symfony's IsGranted attribute denies access (403) unless the required role/permission is held.
Symfony voters implement authorization checks on specific objects via the security checker, e.g. isGranted('EDIT', $post).
Symfony 7 removed support for Doctrine annotations, so validation constraints must use PHP attributes.
Symfony forms include CSRF protection by default, adding and validating a CSRF token field on submission.
Symfony's form validation always runs on the server when the form is submitted, regardless of any client-side HTML5 validation that may have passed.
The Symfony MakerBundle command make:form generates a form type class.
Symfony stores the encoded (hashed) password in the session security token, not the plain-text password.
Symfony loads YAML configuration from config/packages, conventionally one file per bundle or topic.
In Symfony best practice, .env contains non-sensitive dev defaults and is committed, while .env.local holds real secrets and is excluded via .gitignore.
The `bin/console debug:container` command lists registered services and their aliases in the service container.
The compiled container is frozen at runtime, so setParameter cannot be used from a controller.
Since Symfony 3.4/4.0, services are private by default and can only be accessed via dependency injection, not fetched directly from the container.
Bundles work with their default configuration; config files are only needed to override defaults.
In Symfony, environment variables are injected into services.yaml parameters using the %env(VAR)% syntax.
Symfony uses the APP_DEBUG environment variable (typically set in .env) to enable or disable debug mode, including the profiler and Twig debugging.
A message can have multiple handlers; Symfony Messenger calls all handlers registered for a message's bus.

In Symfony Messenger, retry_strategy can be configured separately for each transport via the retry_strategy option under that transport's configuration.

Symfony Messenger allows adding custom middleware to the stack before or after the built-in middleware like validation and handling.
